verdict: APPROVE THE SOURCE FOR THE PINNED SDK BUILD. The implementation follows DESIGN002 and enforces M1, M2 and M4 in code. I found no blocking defect. Notes N1-N4 are non-blocking; N1 is a harness coverage gap that I closed with a scratch-only poll test. This is source review only: SDK compile/link/imports, KC/RAM/host/gate binding, real IOKit concurrency, HID parsing and runtime remain separate gates.

verified_against_design.admission: probe still requires pdm1kbd=1 and pdm1trackpadenum=1, as T1 did. A present pdm1trackpadchild token with any value other than 1 refuses before the CAS. t2Enabled is set only for the exact closed triple; with no token the bundle behaves as T1.
verified_against_design.parent_staging_L1: On T2, start() retains its provider, sets 'RegisterService' to kOSBooleanFalse with exact readback, and publishes the uncommitted state (on parent and IOResources) before allocating the transport. Any failure faults T2, disposes and returns false. After super::start succeeds, T2 diverges into startT2 before published=true or the timer arm. The legacy path is unchanged apart from disposeTransport on a failed workLoop allocation (an existing idempotent path).
verified_against_design.child_preparation: prepareChild requires result ENUM_OK, stage COMPLETE, mask 31, interface 2, descriptor_payload_bytes 110, and a full 110-byte equality against the private reference. trackpad_reference.h holds exactly the attempt-002 descriptor (110 bytes, sha256 4ae5bc26); the reference is used only in the equality guard. initWithSnapshot copies the acquired bytes, sets PDM1SPIInterfaceID = OSNumber(2,32) and RegisterService=false, each with identity readback, plus Built-In and HIDDefaultBehavior. attach then start run outside the gate, before the timer arm, and child start refuses unless the staging property reads back. Any failure: childFault, then rollbackChild, which moves ownership to a local, clears fields, stops only if started (a failed base start already self-stopped through the private-stop guard), detaches and releases. If the keyboard can continue, that becomes the keyboard-only fallback.
verified_against_design.commit: commitT2Gated refuses if stopping, already committed, missing preallocated commit data, or the prepared child is not started or is inactive. It then arms the 2 ms timer (a fallible step, with no state change on failure), takes the permanent parent pin and child pin plus markCommitted, sets phase 1 and published, installs the sink only for a started, unfaulted child, and installs the preallocated committed record. An install failure is a runtime childFault, never a rollback. A commit failure leads to childFault, rollbackChild and the guarded stop, and returns false having registered neither device. On success, parent registerService(async) runs only if phase is still 1, then child registerService(async) only if it is still admitting and active. There is no false return afterward.
verified_against_design.routing: poll is gated on phase 1 at entry and around each received message. Dev1 is unchanged (m1kbd_keyboard_input plus the parent handleReport, wrapped in retain and dispatch counting on T2). Dev2 with flags 0x20 and command 0x10 goes to routeTrackpad: m1tp_child_input requires ID = payload[0] and exact lengths (02,8), (3f,17), (44,1752); other IDs and lengths are counted and consumed with no fault. With no sink the message is consumed. A non-admitting or inactive child is retired recursively (the M3 hardening). The report is copied before the next dlsp_push and submitted through synchronous child->handleReport with both owners retained. An allocation or submit error is a child-only fault, so the keyboard continues. Base IOHIDDevice sets _readyForInputReports at child start after the parse (IOHIDDevice.cpp:418), so the window between commit and registration cannot return kIOReturnOffline, and WORKLOOP_LOCK uses the event source's own loop.
verified_against_design.M1: Parent handleOpen and newUserClient refuse only when t2Enabled and (phase != 1 or inactive), using an atomic read and no gate. Legacy calls go straight to super. Userspace IOServiceOpen reaches the virtual 5-argument newUserClient (IOUserClient.cpp:4463), which IOHIDDevice overrides (IOHIDDevice.cpp:894), so the guard intercepts every open. The child handleOpen requires admitting and active, and the child newUserClient always returns Unsupported.
verified_against_design.M2: Child willTerminate, stop and handleStop close the atomic admission (markRetired), then clearProviderSink calls parent->retireChild, a recursive runAction on the inherited gate. Nothing waits, sleeps or drains. retireChild returns if the gate is gone, and on runAction failure it only removes state (admission is already closed). stopT2Gated and retireChildGated only flip state, cancel the timer and republish.
verified_against_design.M4: There is no PDM1SPITrackpad::getWorkLoop and no async report API. Delivery uses base handleReport with the retained _workLoop and _eventSource. The harness asserts that after detach getWorkLoop() is NULL while _workLoop is still the loop, and that later stops do not touch it.
verified_against_design.L3_retention: Once committed, both stop() wrappers, both handleStop() overrides, disposeTransport, quiesce, rollbackChild and both free() overrides refuse destructive work and log TEARDOWN_DEFERRED or an invariant violation, with no resurrection. The pins plus childOwned make committed free unreachable through balanced releases (harness: refs stay at least 1 and nothing is freed after release sequences). fail() may still call the bounded m1kbd_hw_stop.
verified_against_design.state_record: child_state.h asserts size 32 and every offset. publishChildState removes all three copies before allocating a new immutable OSData; a partial install failure removes all copies, so no stale ready record remains. The original last_error is preserved across later faults. The fallback tuple is committed 1, route_ready 0, faulted 1 with a nonzero error.
verified_against_design.passive: Both getReport/setReport overloads on the child return Unsupported locally and queue no completion. The frozen startHardware, enumerate, enumerateTrackpad, waitResponse, receive and preserveTrackpadEnumeration bodies are byte-identical to T1 (harness check). There are no new request keys and no feature, output, haptic or dimension path.

independent_checks.verify_source.py: 23 files verified, set b70540ba, patch replayed onto sdk-build-inputs-002 and reproduces every owned file.
independent_checks.test_child.py: Run with TMPDIR in my scratch: 5/5 OK. The startup failure sweep covers 37 boundaries, with real extracted parent bodies plus the complete child TU against the fake IOKit. Also: policy and real fragment engine including a fragmented 1752-byte report; NDEBUG refused for both programs; all 7 mutants killed (parent_staging, parent_stop, parent_dispose, parent_free, child_stop, legacy_open, length_minimum); frozen-transport fidelity and forbidden-call scans.
independent_checks.scratch_poll_extension: Not part of the frozen harness; no repository file touched. Using root's stage() and the real extracted PDM1SPIHID::poll/routeTrackpad: T2 committed with mixed traffic sends dev1 only to the parent keyboard and exact 0x02 and 0x44 to the child, rejects a 9-byte 0x02 and unknown ID 0x55 (rejected 2), keeps a dev2 command-0x20 envelope as an other-message, and leaves t2Dispatches at 0. After the committed stop, poll consumes and delivers nothing. In the keyboard-only fallback, dev2 is consumed and counted but never delivered while the keyboard is delivered. In legacy mode dev2 is an other-message and never counted as child traffic. PASS (host fake only).

notes.text: The frozen harness never executes PDM1SPIHID::poll. lifecycle_main.cpp defines 'incoming' and a fake receive() but never fills them, so the T2 changes in poll (phase gates, keyboard dispatch accounting, dev2 branch placement) are covered only by reading. DESIGN002 tests 5 and 7 ask for keyboard dispatch and 'dev1 never reaches the child'. My scratch extension covers them and passes. Recommend adding equivalent poll cases in a later harness revision; this does not block the SDK build.

The legacy path sets PDM1KeyboardPhase='descriptor-published-awaiting-input' after the timer arm; startT2 never sets it, so a committed T2 keyboard keeps 'controller-ready'. No safety impact. Qualifiers and inventories must not expect the legacy phase string in T2.

commitT2Gated returns NotReady, so the whole parent start fails, if a prepared child became inactive before commit, instead of committing a keyboard-only fallback. That fails closed with no registration and is consistent with DESIGN002's 'verify prepared state'. Noted only because step 5's fallback otherwise prefers keeping the keyboard.

Still runtime-only: real IOKit arbitration and concurrency, IOHIDDevice parsing of the 110-byte descriptor with a 1752-byte report, interface and event-driver attachment, and kind-2 queue publication. The receipt's limits list these correctly.
